paper.title_en: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
paper.abstract_en: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.
